liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alligator Reprise** (3 reviews): Around nine minutes, Alligator sounds like an early version of Darkness Jam; The Alligator, Drums, Jam, Alligator reprise sequence is called the best rendition the reviewer has heard [8][11][17]
- **Caution** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out Caution as excellent; Caution contains a There Is A Mountain theme [5][13]
- **Feedback** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls Feedback the most inspired they have heard, with everyone contributing; Feedback takes a few minutes to shed the preceding busy music, then becomes sonically rewarding and exploratory [14][16]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums is mind-bending, with Pigpen screaming and pounding his organ keys [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Alligator Reprise**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [18]
- **Mountain Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 4 archived performances [18]
- **Caution Reprise**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-05-18.aud.goodbear.50.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 7 songs; 41 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd68-05-18.aud.jools.18216.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 6 songs; 41 min; rated 4.53/5 by 15 [2]. Said about its sound: Like most audience tapes, the air can be reduced by lowering the 8K EQ level; Reviewer calls the audience recording muddy [11][13]
- **gd1968-05-18.aud.dad.82515.flac16**: audience recording; 6 songs; 40 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Reasonable for 1968, though Pigpen's vocals are hard to hear; The first few seconds of Alligator are missing from this transfer [3][15]
- **gd1968-05-18.aud.kaukonen.11796.shnf**: audience recording; 5 songs; 41 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [4]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Jorma and Others, WEIR, JORMA, CASSIDY & ? [1]
- Weir delivers a profane rant after Feedback, repeatedly shouting about the proletariat [6]
- Weir can be heard going off about the proles backstage [9]
- Reviewer comments on the backstage interview track as amusing [15]
- Track 6 contains Bob Weir talking to Jorma backstage [3]
- Jorma can be heard talking with Bob Weir on track 6 [4]
- Afternoon concert on a bill with the Doors, Animals, Big Brother, Youngbloods, Electric Flag, Jefferson Airplane, Kaleidoscope, Country Joe, Taj Mahal [5]
- The Dead played the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles later that evening [5]
- Reviewer says the grungy sound is still better than the 6/14/68 recording [6]
- Reviewer finds the mix better overall than the 6-14 tape and thinks May and June 1968 playing was ferocious [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-05-18.aud.goodbear.50.shnf**: taped by Jorma masters with stage mics - unknown gen]; transferred by Teddy Goodbear; source: MAC > ? > SHN [1]
- **gd68-05-18.aud.jools.18216.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Julian (Jools) Elliott; source: Audience [2]. Also: Reviewer suspects this is Jorma's onstage recording rather than Tom's audience tape, citing deadlists about the backstage speech; Jorma taped parts of the show for his own interest; Two audience masters circulate: Tom Ordon's mono handheld-mic reel recording, and a supposed Jorma stage-mic one; uploader unsure which this is [2][7][11]
- **gd1968-05-18.aud.dad.82515.flac16**: taped by Jorma Kaukonen; source: JORMA'S AUD MASTER > 3RD GEN CASSETTE > CD [3]. Also: Chain runs from Jorma's audience master to a third-generation cassette, then CD, with Soundforge and Cool Edit processing [3]
- **gd1968-05-18.aud.kaukonen.11796.shnf**: taped by Jorma Kaukonen; source: AUD > ? > CD [4]. Also: Jorma Kaukonen recorded it with onstage microphones [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1968-05-18 Grateful Dead Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1968-05-18-grateful-dead-poster-2/) [19]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1968-05-18 Grateful Dead Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1968-05-18-grateful-dead-poster-2/) [20]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Santa Clara County Fairgrounds - May 18, 1968](https://www.dead.net/show/may-18-1968) [21]
